finding: The random-field XXZ data use one second-order product-formula substep per record interval, but no convergence study is part of the release.
evidence: Model registry sets dt_record=0.25 and trotter_substeps=1. Independent n=10,12 tests against 8 substeps found normalized metric errors up to 0.576 and substantial changes in metric-competition rates.
impact: XXZ-specific path morphology, competition rates, and any physical interpretation as XXZ Hamiltonian dynamics are not numerically controlled.
action: Regenerate XXZ with at least 4 substeps and demonstrate 4-vs-8 convergence at n=10,12,14; preferably regenerate all release sizes. Otherwise relabel the object as a fixed product-formula circuit and remove claims of converged XXZ dynamics.
gate: Max declared-observable 4-vs-8 differences below a preregistered tolerance; regenerated tables/figures/tests all pass.
release_disposition: Blocker closed under the fixed-circuit interpretation.
residual_action: A future Hamiltonian-dynamics dataset should use the convergence-controlled setting over all desired sizes.

finding: The documented make rebuild-included workflow does not feed its freshly recomputed robustness results into the public figure builder.
evidence: scripts/rebuild_all_from_included_data.sh writes outputs/rebuild/* and then calls scripts/build_public_figures.py, while that builder always reads data/public_analysis_inputs.zip.
impact: The public figures can remain unchanged even when a fresh analysis differs, so the advertised end-to-end provenance chain is not real.
action: Add an explicit input directory/archive option to the figure builder and use fresh outputs, or fail unless fresh tables match the archived public inputs within declared tolerances.
gate: A controlled perturbation of a recomputed table changes the corresponding figure or causes the workflow to fail.
release_disposition: End-to-end public-figure provenance implemented and tested.

finding: The code claims an exact q=0 Rényi/Hartley limit but uses a numerical support threshold that contradicts the documented exact discontinuity.
evidence: At d=1024 and p=1-1e-14, the equal-tail spectrum has 1024 strictly positive entries and exact H0=10 bits, but the default code and fixed-p boundary return H0=0 because support_tol=1e-15.
impact: The repository's stated exact all-q metric layer is false at q=0 near product spectra.
action: Implement Hartley fixed-p boundaries analytically and distinguish exact mathematical support from numerical-rank estimation; add near-product regression tests.
gate: The d=1024,p=1-1e-14 counterexample returns lower=1 bit, upper=10 bits (base 2), and exact constructed spectra do not use a positive support threshold.
release_disposition: Exact Hartley and thresholded numerical rank are separated.

finding: Dependencies are specified only by lower bounds and no passing hosted run for the final release commit was verified during this audit.
evidence: pyproject.toml permits arbitrary future NumPy, pandas, SciPy, matplotlib, Pillow, PyYAML, and pytest versions. A previous hosted run exposed backend/version sensitivity.
impact: A tagged release may not reproduce its own figures and numerical tolerances across environments.
action: Add a release constraints/lock file and make the primary CI job install it; optionally retain a second latest-dependencies portability job. Require a green run on the tagged commit.
gate: Clean hosted CI passes using the pinned release environment and reports package versions.
release_disposition: Exact release locks and a hardened pinned CI job are present; local structure and scientific checks pass.
residual_action: Require one green locked hosted workflow run on the final uploaded commit before tagging.

finding: The strongest fingerprint/classification numbers use the full path and are substantially boosted by the shared horizontal lambda_max coordinate.
evidence: Centroid leave-size same/cross accuracy is 0.917/0.694 for full paths but 0.806/0.347 for vertical-only paths. Individual double-holdout vertical-only cross-metric accuracy is 0.257.
impact: Readers may attribute common-x information to metric-robust vertical morphology.
action: Show full-path, vertical-only, and lambda_max-only results together in Figure 5 and its caption; lead with the y-only result when discussing cross-metric transfer.
gate: Public claims and figure distinguish shared-coordinate signal from metric-dependent signal.
release_disposition: Figure 5 and docs separate full-path, vertical-only, and lambda-max-only classification.

finding: Trajectory resampling bridges internal intervals where the boundary-relative coordinate is undefined.
evidence: The interpolation keeps all finite samples between the first and last finite time, even across internal NaN gaps. QCA_1 has 12-21 internal missing points depending on size.
impact: Some distances and classifications are computed through artificial interpolation across collapsed exact envelopes.
action: Interpolate only within contiguous finite segments or report a gap-aware sensitivity analysis in the canonical outputs.
gate: Gap-aware results are primary or shown alongside current values; no hidden bridging of undefined intervals.
release_disposition: Boundary-coordinate interpolation is contiguous-segment and gap aware.

finding: The phrase four quantum-chaos families overstates the status of all included conditions.
evidence: The registry includes Clifford-reference QCA, transverse-reference kicked Ising, standard/perturbed baker, and weak/strong-disorder XXZ conditions; chaos is not established separately for every run.
impact: The empirical scope can be read as a controlled comparison of four chaotic ensembles when it is a broader dynamics suite.
action: Use four dynamical families used to probe scrambling, integrability, localization, and spectral complexity unless a chaos diagnostic is supplied per condition.
gate: README, AI context, captions, and metadata use scoped terminology consistently.
release_disposition: Public claim wording now says four dynamical families used to probe scrambling, recurrence, disorder, and spectral complexity.
residual_action: Retain quantum-chaos as a discovery keyword, not a per-condition classification.

finding: Each model-condition-size cell is deterministic and the study has only four designed conditions per model, not independent ensemble replication.
evidence: One deterministic random-product seed and one disorder realization are used per applicable run and size.
impact: Bootstrap intervals and classifier accuracy describe the designed dataset, not a population of disorder or initial-state realizations.
action: State this prominently; call the bootstrap a design-cluster sensitivity interval. For stronger model inference, add independent disorder and initial-state replicates.
gate: No population-level language without genuine replicate ensembles.
release_disposition: Designed deterministic conditions and nonpopulation interpretation are explicit; model-stratified design-cluster sensitivity is canonical.
residual_action: Independent disorder/initial-state replicates remain a future expansion, not a v1.0.0 claim.

finding: The common coordinate tau=step/n is not a universal physical time across the four model families.
evidence: Simulation records tau=step/n, whereas XXZ has dt_record=0.25 and circuit/map iterations have different physical meanings.
impact: Cross-model trajectory geometry can be interpreted as time-aligned physical dynamics when it is a scaled iteration/depth coordinate.
action: Rename tau to scaled step or scaled depth in public text and retain model-specific physical-time metadata.
gate: All figures/captions define the coordinate without implying universal physical time.
release_disposition: Tau is defined as a scaled iteration coordinate, not common physical time.

finding: The corrected repository lacks a consolidated peer-review bibliography for its exact and interpretive claims.
evidence: Core documents invoke majorization, Page entropy, Li-Haldane, Wishart/MP, and product-formula physics without a stable REFERENCES.md or equivalent full citations.
impact: Readers and AI systems cannot easily distinguish established results from this repository's derivations and interpretations.
action: Add primary references with DOI/arXiv links and map them to claim IDs.
gate: Every external theorem or historical attribution has a complete primary citation.
release_disposition: Primary references and machine-readable bibliography added.
residual_action: Keep bibliography current in future releases.

finding: The cluster bootstrap samples 16 model-condition units without stratifying by model.
evidence: A model-stratified cluster bootstrap gives a similar but conceptually cleaner PC1 CI [0.861,0.934] versus the released [0.857,0.938].
impact: The reported interval can fluctuate in model composition and should not be interpreted as a balanced four-model uncertainty interval.
action: Use model-stratified cluster resampling or explicitly label the current interval as an unstratified design sensitivity.
gate: Bootstrap unit, target population, and stratification are explicit.
release_disposition: Canonical interval is model-stratified over designed condition clusters and labeled a sensitivity interval.

finding: PUBLIC_FIGURE_STORY.md advertises supplemental random-matrix figure files that are absent from the repository.
evidence: It names figures/public/supplemental/figure_reference_01_distance_n20.* and figure_spectrum_04_endpoint_scorecard_n20.*, but the directory is absent.
impact: Broken provenance expectations and misleading navigation.
action: Remove the section or include the files and registry entries.
gate: All documented public files exist.
release_disposition: Absent supplemental figure claims removed.

finding: data/README.md says the three data objects are checksum-tracked after the checksum records were intentionally deleted.
evidence: The opening sentence retains checksum-tracked wording.
impact: Small but direct factual inconsistency.
action: Replace with version-controlled or bundled data objects.
gate: No stale checksum language.
release_disposition: Stale checksum-tracked wording removed.

finding: CORRECTIONS.md has duplicated and nonexistent machine-record claims and future-tense wording.
evidence: It lists paper_correction_ledger.csv twice and says equation/figure dispositions are available in CSV and JSON although those compact files are absent; it says What the repository will say.
impact: Weakens the authority of the correction layer.
action: Correct the machine-readable record paragraph and use present tense.
gate: Every linked/claimed correction artifact exists and is unique.
release_disposition: Correction record now points only to existing unique artifacts and uses present tense.

finding: Saved NPZ spectra are stored in ascending eigvalsh order although the canonical Schmidt-spectrum convention is descending.
evidence: All 405 spectra are valid but raw arrays are ascending; current metric code silently normalizes/sorts them on read.
impact: External users can misread lambda_1 and leading-edge diagnostics if they inspect the archive directly.
action: Repackage spectra in canonical descending order or document an explicit archive-order field and loader requirement.
gate: Archive schema and actual ordering agree.
release_disposition: Selected spectra are repacked in descending order with explicit schema metadata.

finding: Some coarse descriptor language overstates what is measured.
evidence: Arc length includes the common lambda_max coordinate; signed polygonal area does not close the last-to-first segment. Vertical-only total-variation rank correlations are lower than full-path arc-length correlations.
impact: Fine/coarse geometry can appear more metric-robust because of the shared x coordinate or ambiguous area convention.
action: Report x-only/y-only/full descriptors separately and rename the area to the actual open-path line-integral/origin-closed convention.
gate: Descriptor formulas and interpretation match exactly.
release_disposition: Descriptors now distinguish full-path arc length, vertical total variation, origin-closed area, and exact turns.

finding: The general scientific validator still contains browser-upload packaging limits.
evidence: It fails above 100 files or 25 MiB, constraints unrelated to scientific correctness after the repository is established.
impact: Legitimate future documentation/tests can break CI for non-scientific reasons.
action: Move packaging-size checks to a separate release-packaging command.
gate: Scientific CI and packaging CI are independent.
release_disposition: Browser-upload size limits removed from scientific validation.
residual_action: Packaging constraints may be handled separately if needed.

finding: Pure-state logarithmic negativity is materially more sensitive to tiny numerical tails than other stored metrics.
evidence: Reconstruction of 405 spectra agrees to 1.71e-7 for log negativity versus about 1e-13 for VN/linear and 1e-14 for leading-eigenvalue metrics.
impact: Uniform precision language would be misleading.
action: Declare metric-specific tolerances and preserve raw eigenvalue-cleaning conventions.
gate: QA tables report per-metric tolerances.
release_disposition: Metric-specific numerical tolerances and tail sensitivity are documented and tested.

finding: The repository description is set, but the DOI homepage and topics remain unset and GitHub labels the mixed license file as Other.
evidence: Current repository API reports empty homepage, topics=[], license=Other.
impact: Reduced discoverability and ambiguous sidebar presentation.
action: Set DOI homepage and topics; optionally split the standard BSD text into LICENSE and the CC-BY notice into LICENSE-CONTENT.md.
gate: Repository API exposes homepage/topics and a clear license presentation.
release_disposition: Standard BSD code license and separate CC-BY content notice are present; GitHub description is set.
residual_action: Set DOI homepage, topics, and social preview in GitHub before tagging. GitHub license sidebar behavior should be checked visually.

finding: The objective errors in the published paper are material enough that a repository clarification alone does not amend the version of record.
evidence: The correction ledger includes the exact entropy boundary, Page formula, rank-one spike, QFT invariance, Wishart scaling, and other factual corrections.
impact: Readers using only the journal article can continue to encounter incorrect statements.
action: After freezing the corrected release, submit a concise factual corrigendum to Quantum.
gate: Journal correspondence initiated; repository accurately states its status.
release_disposition: Repository correction layer is frozen and explicitly does not amend the journal version of record.
residual_action: Submit a concise factual corrigendum to Quantum after v1.0.0 is frozen.

finding: Only five selected n=20 runs have complete spectra and the selection omits some important families/conditions.
evidence: Archive contains KI_3, KI_4, QCA_2, XXZ_2, and XXZ_4; no baker spectrum and no non-Clifford QCA spectrum.
impact: The 400-transition majorization audit is a selected-case mechanism check, not a model-wide frequency estimate.
action: Keep that limitation prominent or expand the spectrum sample.
gate: No model-wide majorization-frequency claim from the selected archive.
release_disposition: Selected-spectrum audit is explicitly described as a five-run mechanism check, not a model-wide frequency estimate.
residual_action: Expand spectra to omitted families only for a future model-wide frequency claim.
